walkthroughs.body_html:
Investigating Small Business — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Investigating Small Business brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Investigating Small Business.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does the 'S' in SMART objectives stand for?
options: Strategic
Specific
Strong
Saleable

mcqs.q: Which 1970 essay argued the 'social responsibility of business is to increase profits'?
options: Drucker
Porter
Friedman
Carroll

mcqs.q: Do most new business ideas come from brand-new inventions?
options: You can only start a business if you invent something completely new.
Business risk is automatically insured by banks.
No — most come from spotting gaps in existing markets, adapting existing products, or responding to changes in technology and consumer wants.
New business ideas are allocated to entrepreneurs by the government.

mcqs.q: Is risk something entrepreneurs should always avoid?
options: Good entrepreneurs eliminate all risk before starting.
New business ideas are allocated to entrepreneurs by the government.
Business risk is automatically insured by banks.
No — enterprise involves weighing risk against reward; successful entrepreneurs take calculated risks and reduce them through market research and planning.

mcqs.q: Does a business plan guarantee a start-up will succeed?
options: No — a plan reduces risk by forcing research on customers, costs and cash flow, and helps obtain finance, but markets and assumptions can still change.
Business plans are legal contracts with customers.
Business risk is automatically insured by banks.
Writing a business plan ensures the business will work.
